hero.title: Your Founder Commitment.
hero.intro: Bring your purpose, responsibilities, and support plan into a realistic four-week commitment. Choose small actions, protect your time, and decide how you will review what you learn.

fields.label: What will you commit to learning over four weeks?
fields.placeholder: Understand how event visitors follow up and document the questions that remain.
fields.hint: Connect your purpose to a useful learning goal within your influence.

fields.label: What schedule and resource boundary can you realistically keep?
fields.placeholder: Tuesday evening, up to two hours a week, no paid tools for this learning step.
fields.hint: Include when, weekly time limit, and any resource limit.

fields.label: Week 1 — action, output and review point
fields.placeholder: Observe one situation, record five notes and questions, review Friday.
fields.hint: Choose one useful starting action and what you can show afterwards.

fields.label: Week 2 — action, output and review point
fields.placeholder: Draft three neutral questions, rehearse, keep revisions, review Friday.
fields.hint: Build on Week 1 without assuming research has already happened.

fields.label: Week 3 — action, output and review point
fields.placeholder: Arrange suitable discovery conversations with permission; keep actual notes or an access log; review Friday.
fields.hint: State any access/permission dependency and how you will handle it.

fields.label: Week 4 — action, output and review point
fields.placeholder: Summarise observations and uncertainty; choose the next learning step; review the plan Friday.
fields.hint: Plan a synthesis and next decision rather than promising commercial results.

fields.label: How will you review actual progress and choose the next step?
fields.placeholder: Each Friday record what happened, what remains unknown and whether to continue, simplify, change or pause.
fields.hint: Compare plan vs actual, record learning/uncertainty, and specify continue/change/pause criteria.

fields.label: What is your minimum useful action and fallback?
fields.placeholder: If only 20 minutes remain, refine one question; if support is unavailable, revise with the guide and review the schedule.
fields.hint: Describe a smaller action for a difficult week and a boundary that triggers adjustment.

fields.label: What support or dependency should remain visible?
fields.placeholder: Optional: planned peer review, access still needed, or an unresolved constraint…

fields.label: Which part depends on an assumption or unavailable resource?
fields.placeholder: I am assuming… It is not yet confirmed because…

fields.label: What evidence will show useful learning rather than just activity?
fields.placeholder: I can show… I will keep observations separate from…

fields.label: What would make you simplify, change, or pause the plan?
fields.placeholder: If… happens by… I will adjust the plan by…

questions.prompt: What should a four-week founder commitment describe?
options: A guarantee that the business will succeed
A realistic learning goal, schedule, weekly outputs and review points
A promise that all possible supporters will help
questions.explanation: Commit to practical learning within your influence, not guaranteed venture outcomes.

questions.prompt: When your week becomes too busy, what is a useful response?
options: Choose a smaller useful action and review the plan
questions.explanation: Adapt the scope honestly instead of inventing progress or adding unsustainable commitments.

options: You completed starter work and made a learning plan
The venture has received investment approval
questions.explanation: Module completion records learning and deliverables; commercial validation and review decisions are separate.

scenes.title: Make the commitment practical
scenes.visual: Founder brings a notebook, calendar and simple task notes together in a Dubai workspace.
scenes.narration: You have explored your starting point, responsibilities, motivation and support needs. Now turn them into a commitment you can actually keep. This is a four-week learning plan, not a promise of business success. Start with the time and resources you really have.

scenes.title: Protect a realistic schedule
scenes.visual: Calendar blocks assembled as editable graphics; founder chooses one small working session.
scenes.narration: Choose a weekly time limit and a regular session. Make room for your other responsibilities. A small plan you can repeat is more useful than a large promise you cannot sustain. If you are unsure, start modestly and review after the first week.

scenes.title: Give each week a useful output
scenes.visual: Four editable week cards, observation notebook, neutral questions and a peer practice moment.
scenes.narration: For each week, name an action, an output and a review point. You might first observe a situation, then prepare questions, practise with a peer, and review the clues you have collected. Adapt the sequence to your context. Planned conversations are not completed research, and notes are not proof of demand.

scenes.title: Review what happened
scenes.visual: Editable plan-versus-observation diagram, founder checks notes without success metrics.
scenes.narration: At your review, compare the plan with what actually happened. What did you learn? What remains uncertain? Choose whether to continue, simplify, change direction or pause. Keep your observations separate from assumptions. Completing your schedule does not mean your venture has been validated.

scenes.title: Plan for a difficult week
scenes.visual: Founder reduces a calendar block; simple minimum-action and fallback cards appear in post.
scenes.narration: A useful commitment includes a fallback. If time or support is unavailable, choose the smallest action that still helps you learn. Set a resource boundary and a point to stop or ask for help. Missing a session is a reason to adjust the plan, not to invent progress.

blocks.prompt:
Create an engaging beginner-friendly explainer for LYNQ Venture Studio Academy, Module 1.1 Lesson 05: “Your Founder Commitment.” Desired final edit: approximately 150 seconds, 16:9, 1080p. Use natural documentary workplace shots, simple editable calendar/weekly-plan diagrams and an actual worksheet screen recording. Navy #0B2338, teal #087D79, mint #BCF2DF and white. Contemporary Dubai workspace, diverse adults, calm supportive plain-language English narrator. No dramatic success imagery or motivational pressure.

Teaching goals: turn the first four lessons into a realistic four-week learning commitment; define weekly time limits and action/output/review points; distinguish planned work from completed evidence; choose continue/simplify/change/pause decisions; and create a fallback for a busy week. No promises of revenue, business validation, investment, certification or personal transformation. Use a fictional aspiring founder exploring event visitors' follow-up experiences. Label the example “Illustrative example.” No invented customers, interviews, metrics or confirmed collaborators.

Use the six scenes below in order. Target about 25 seconds per final scene, adjusting after a narrator read-through and allowing natural diagram holds. Record one consistent voice track separately. Generate short visual shots only in durations supported by the selected Gemini/Veo account/model; an eight-second shot plan is optional where supported. Assemble clips, diagrams, captions and narration in an editor rather than claiming a single generation produces the whole film.

Return a storyboard, shot prompts, narration timing and editing instructions first. Generated footage must contain no text, logos, captions, watermark, speaking presenters or fabricated product UI. Keep continuity with the same approved actor reference and wardrobe. Exact LYNQ branding and diagrams must be added as editable post-production graphics. Suggested graphics: When + Time limit + Action; Week 1 / Week 2 / Week 3 / Week 4 with Action → Output → Review; Planned ≠ Observed; Continue / Simplify / Change / Pause; Five Module 1.1 deliverables.

Scene 6 must use a genuine screen recording of the approved Lesson 05 worksheet with fictional data; never generate the interface or show private founder information. Module completion means local curriculum self-completion, not a certificate or venture-readiness approval. Finish with editable end card: “Make a realistic commitment. Take the next small step.”

Human production deliverables: H.264 1920×1080 MP4, editable project and graphics, narrator audio, thumbnail, timed English VTT/SRT and transcript, reference rights/generation provenance. Provide separately native-reviewed Arabic narration/captions and RTL diagrams; do not auto-mirror English UI. Review mobile caption legibility, natural pacing, audio intelligibility, curriculum accuracy, progress wording and brand before publication. No video is generated by the prototype.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Commit to learning, with room to adapt.

children: A founder commitment is a practical agreement with yourself about what you will do next. It connects your purpose to actions you can control. It should fit your time, responsibilities and resources.

You are not promising to build a successful company in four weeks. You are choosing a repeatable way to explore, learn and review. Changing or pausing an approach can be responsible progress when the evidence or your circumstances call for it.
By the end, you can
Set a realistic weekly schedule and resource boundary.
Plan four weeks with a clear action, output and review point.
Separate intended work from observed evidence.
Choose a fallback when a week does not go to plan.
Bring together your five Module 1.1 deliverables.
Bring your earlier work with you
Lesson 01 · Starting point
Use the interests, strengths and time commitment from your Founder Profile.
Review Founder Profile
Lesson 02 · Useful work
Choose the next action from your Responsibility Map rather than filling the schedule with busy work.
Review Responsibility Map
Lesson 03 · Direction & habits
Use your purpose, repeatable habit and boundary. Keep the purpose open to learning.
Review Purpose & Learning Plan
Lesson 04 · Capability & support
Plan around your priority gap and available support. Do not treat a planned request as confirmed help.
Review Skills & Support Map
Choose a schedule you can protect

Name when you will work and the maximum time or resources you will use. If your week is already full, begin with a short session and one useful output. A calendar entry is a plan; it is not evidence that the work happened.
Use action → output → review
Action:
what you will do.
Output:
something you can show afterwards, such as notes or a revised question list.
Review:
when you will compare the result with the plan and decide what to do next.
Illustrative four-week plan:
Week 1: observe one event situation; record observations and unanswered questions; review Friday.
Week 2: draft three neutral questions and rehearse; keep a revised question list; review Friday.
Week 3: where appropriate and with permission, arrange a few discovery conversations; record actual notes or access limitations; review Friday.
Week 4: summarise clues and uncertainty; choose the next learning step; review the whole plan.
This is one example, not a required pace or proof of customer demand.

blocks.prompt: You planned two hours, but now have only 20 minutes. Which response best preserves honest learning?

options.label: Mark the planned work complete anyway
options.feedback: Keep the record honest and the commitment realistic. Choose a smaller useful action rather than marking unfinished work complete or adding more commitments.

options.label: Choose a smaller useful action and review the plan
options.feedback: Useful choice: reduce the scope to something that still helps you learn, then review the schedule. Record what actually happened; planned work is not completed work.

options.label: Add more commitments to catch up
options.feedback: Keep the record honest and the commitment realistic. Choose a smaller useful action rather than marking unfinished work complete or adding more commitments.

children: Optional practice, separate from the scored quiz.
Review without pretending

Ask what you actually did, what you learned, what still needs checking, and which action is useful next. Record missed work honestly. If your plan needs unavailable people or resources, simplify it, choose another suitable source, or pause.
Learning completion is not venture validation.
Finishing Module 1.1 gives you a starter pack and a plan. It does not prove demand, guarantee funding, or approve a business opportunity.

Create a four-week learning plan you can adapt. Each week needs an action, an output, and a review point. If you have no business idea yet, commit to observing and exploring rather than inventing one.
Arabic entries use automatic text direction. Use roles or aliases for other people. This lesson saves separately from Lessons 01–04.
This is your draft commitment, not a signed contract or externally approved plan. Local storage is plaintext; download a copy before changing browsers.
Simulated Coach · no AI connection
Try four scripted guidance modes. The preview reads your current worksheet locally; it does not send information anywhere.
